f_h_hz.name: f_h_hz
f_h_hz.method: saturated VMAC issue rate; CHAINS sweep 1/2/4/8, ITERS slope fit on npu_time
evidence: plateau: 1.015/1.019/1.013 G VMAC/s at chains=2/4/8 (within 0.6%) -> pipe saturated, latency hidden
chains=1 (1.92 ns/iter) == chains=2 (1.97 ns/iter): 1 chain is latency-bound, 2 fill the pipe
chains=4 -> 8 throughput ratio 0.994x: plateau, not still-scaling
disassembly (llvm-objdump, aie2): loop .LBB0_1 unrolled 4x (r5=0x3e8=ITERS, add r5,r5,#-0x4); 16 bundles / 16 vmac in body incl. branch delay slots => exactly 1 VMAC per bundle
bundle count x measured slope: 4 cycles/iter / 3.9244 ns = 1.019 GHz, agrees with the plateau independently
caveats: assumes 1 bundle/cycle issue (standard VLIW model); the plateau corroborates but does not prove it
measured at pmode=default; setting pmode needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN. Do not assume clock-invariance across modes.

c_cmd_s.name: c_cmd_s

evidence: across both runs the floor sits in 148.7-162.0 us; point estimate 155 us (+/-5%)
independent corroboration: K1 chains=1 fit intercept ~236 us on a larger graph, same order
caveats: THIS IS THE DOMINANT TERM ON npu1: a do-nothing dispatch costs ~155 us of device time. For scale, R64 measured aie2p full production QKV device span at 241 us.
warmed medians; cold first-command values are far higher (R63 saw 3.5-4.2 ms cold vs 1.03 ms warm)
measured at n_bos 2-3 only; see c_bo_s

c_bo_s.name: c_bo_s
c_bo_s.method: BO-count sweep slope; not separable from noise
evidence: run A slope = -5.130 us/BO (negative => unphysical => noise-dominated)
run B slope = +4.600 us/BO; the sign flips between runs
conclusion: |c_bo| < ~5 us, indistinguishable from zero, and <3% of the 155 us floor

sweep is BLOCKED above n_bos=3: nargs>=3 fails aiecc with "Resource allocation pipeline failed" at tile(0,2) — a core tile cannot source that many input DMA channels. The 5-slot H4 limit is never reached because the per-core DMA channel limit binds first.

c_task_issue_s.name: c_task_issue_s
c_task_issue_s.method: 8 MiB payload held constant; tile-size sweep varies task count 8x (4096 -> 512). Slope of npu_time vs task count.
evidence: fitted slope moved 9.8 ns -> 3.3 ns/task between runs; point estimate 5 ns with the sign stable but the magnitude not

Reason: npu1 feeds at ~3.7 GB/s/column, so a 2 KiB tile takes ~553 ns to move while task issue costs ~5 ns — the overhead hides completely behind the transfer. halo moves bytes ~3.5x faster per column, which is what made per-task cost visible there. Task-count optimisation is NOT a lever on npu1.
value is an upper bound, not a fit: below the noise floor at these sizes
single column; concurrent multi-column issue is unmeasured
tile=32 KiB failed to build: 32 KiB x depth-2 double buffer = 64 KiB = exactly L1 (M1). M1 binds the tile size.

feed marginal 0.327 W = 6.546 mJ/dispatch over 33.6 MB -> 1.9508e-10 J/byte (5.13 GB/J)

caveats: PACKAGE-DELTA basis on an APU: CPU+GPU+NPU share rails and there is no NPU power sensor. Never report as NPU power.

MATCHED RATE IS LOAD-BEARING. Free-running, package power tracks dispatch rate: a null kernel at 4326/s burns 10.343 W doing nothing, vs compute 1.082 W at 133/s. Free-run even INVERTS the ordering (free-run says feed >> compute; matched-rate says compute > feed). Any energy number taken without rate matching is measuring the host submit loop.
measured at pmode=default; f_H is pmode-invariant (turbo is a no-op) but energy may not be
feed = external DDR->array DMA (C2 tile stream). Does not cover memtile->core or core->core movement.

byte_mac_energy_ratio.name: byte_mac_energy_ratio
byte_mac_energy_ratio.method: J/byte divided by J/MAC — the break-even arithmetic intensity
evidence: matched-rate 50 disp/s, 500 dispatches, 10 s windows, RAPL package-0 integration
null 0.337 W / feed 0.664 W / compute 0.773 W package delta; marginals subtract null so host submit cancels
feed marginal 0.327 W = 6.546 mJ/dispatch over 33.6 MB -> 1.9508e-10 J/byte (5.13 GB/J)

caveats: RETIRED — DO NOT USE. ARTIFACT of the 1-core J/MAC. Divided J/byte by 5.32e-12 (1 core, where the fixed 0.36 W dominates) giving 37 MACs/byte. The correct value from the 16-core J/MAC is 183 (int8) / 401 (int4). Use byte_mac_energy_ratio_<dtype_pair>. Retired so no dtype pair can silently fall back to it.
PACKAGE-DELTA basis on an APU: CPU+GPU+NPU share rails and there is no NPU power sensor. Never report as NPU power.

MATCHED RATE IS LOAD-BEARING. Free-running, package power tracks dispatch rate: a null kernel at 4326/s burns 10.343 W doing nothing, vs compute 1.082 W at 133/s. Free-run even INVERTS the ordering (free-run says feed >> compute; matched-rate says compute > feed). Any energy number taken without rate matching is measuring the host submit loop.
measured at pmode=default; f_H is pmode-invariant (turbo is a no-op) but energy may not be
feed = external DDR->array DMA (C2 tile stream). Does not cover memtile->core or core->core movement.

THE tok/J DESIGN LAW: below ~37 MACs per byte fed, energy is dominated by data movement, not arithmetic. Decode (AI~1) is 37x movement-dominated => bit-width is the energy lever. Prefill (AI~M) is compute-dominated => MMUL rate is the energy lever. This is why power-shaped and speed-shaped kernels diverge.

byte_mac_energy_ratio_int8_int8.name: byte_mac_energy_ratio_int8_int8
evidence: J/byte 1.9508e-10 (C2 feed, 4 columns) / J/MAC 16-core measured
int8 x int8: 1.9508e-10 / 1.0659e-12 = 183 MACs per byte
int8 x int4: 1.9508e-10 / 4.8671e-13 = 401 MACs per byte
caveats: SUPERSEDES the 36.7 figure, which divided by the 1-CORE J/MAC (5.32e-12). At 1 core the fixed 0.36 W dominates, making each MAC look 5.5x more expensive than it is at full width. The law was an artifact of an under-parallelised bench.

CONSEQUENCE: prefill (AI 82-101) is NOT compute-dominated as previously stated — it sits well below the 183 break-even, so on npu1 BOTH LLM phases are movement-dominated for energy. The array is simply very efficient (929 G MACs/J) relative to DDR bytes (5.13 GB/J).

batching_tok_j_gain_b512.name: batching_tok_j_gain_b512
batching_tok_j_gain_b512.method: tok/J at B=512 divided by tok/J at B=1, 768x1280 int8 projection, fastest candidate
evidence: 768x1280 projection, int8xint8, int32 out, fastest candidate per batch (npu1):
AI saturates because the OUTPUT scales with batch: byte share w=32%/a=26%/out=43% at B=256
-> w=6%/a=35%/out=59% at B=2048 (int32, 4col); 80% out at 1 col.
only bf16 out AND minimal activation replication crosses 183: B=512 1col bf16 = 187.3; B=2048 1col bf16 = 258.2
caveats: BATCHING IS THE BIGGEST SINGLE LEVER MEASURED: 64x tok/J and 348x tok/s from B=1 to B=512. It amortises WEIGHTS across the batch (weight byte share falls 32% -> 6%).

But batching does NOT amortise the OUTPUT, which scales with batch and comes to dominate the byte count (up to 80%), capping arithmetic intensity around 97-113 with an int32 accumulator. BATCHING ALONE CANNOT CROSS THE 183 BREAK-EVEN.
It also does NOT amortise the KV cache - each sequence carries its own - so decode attention stays movement-bound at ANY batch size. Batch the projections; the KV read is irreducible.

CONSEQUENCE: on npu1 the LLM hot path is movement-bound at every batch size in the practical range, so 'energy is bytes' holds throughout. bf16 output is the cheapest way to buy back both axes (+22% at B=2048), and R65 reached the same conclusion by hand on aie2p.
Model-derived, not measured on hardware: rests on the calibrated J/byte, J/MAC and bw_feed_per_stream.

cpu_gb_per_j.name: cpu_gb_per_j
cpu_gb_per_j.method: 7840HS 16-thread streaming read of 256 MiB, RAPL package delta over idle
evidence: 7840HS, 8 cores / 16 threads, AVX-512 VNNI (_mm512_dpbusd_epi32 = 64 int8 MACs/instr), OpenMP x16
feed:    idle 3.92 W load 41.67 W delta 37.75 W -> 55.83 GB/s, 1.48 GB/J (256 MiB streaming read)
compute: idle 4.09 W load 42.35 W delta 38.26 W -> 2.07 T MACs/s (4.1 TOPS), 54.0 G MACs/J
compute is AT Zen 4 peak: 8 cores x 64 MACs x 4.05 GHz = 2.07e12 exactly (AVX-512 is double-pumped,
so 1 dpbusd/cycle/core is the ceiling; SMT does not help a port-limited op)
same package, same rails, same RAPL counter as E1 (NPU) and G1 (GPU) -> directly comparable
caveats: THE CPU IS DOMINATED ON BOTH AXES: slower than the GPU on feed (55.8 vs 79.5 GB/s) and compute (4.1 vs 15.1 TOPS), and far worse on energy than either (1.48 GB/J vs NPU 5.13; 54 G MACs/J vs NPU 938 — 17x). It is never the throughput-optimal or energy-optimal choice for LLM work on this SoC.

The one thing the CPU beats the NPU at is movement SPEED (55.8 vs 30.8 GB/s) — the NPU is capped by its 8-stream shim ceiling while the CPU has the full DDR path. If a kernel is movement-bound and latency-critical, CPU > NPU on speed, though at 3.5x the energy per byte.
Unlike the GPU compute leg (~42% of theoretical), this is at ~100% of peak, so it is not understated.
No rate-matching needed: E1's confound was the HOST submit loop, and here the host IS the workload.

composition_is_max.name: composition_is_max
composition_is_max.method: stream tiles AND compute per tile; sweep MMULS across the feed/compute crossover
evidence: 1 stream, 1024 x 4 KiB tiles, C1 floor subtracted, per-tile times (npu1):
MMULS   t_core/tile   MEASURED   max model    sum model
mean |error|: max 4.1%, sum 33.2%; max closer on 4/5 points (the 5th is MMULS=0 where both agree)
shape is the prediction: FLAT (1044->1057->1151) while t_core < t_feed, then slope 1
caveats: This validates the model's CENTRAL design decision, which nothing had tested: family B is feed-only (trivial core) and family C is compute-only (no feed). Both terms were validated in ISOLATION; the composition never was.
KNOWN LIMIT: at the crossover (t_core ~= t_feed) the hard max() UNDER-predicts by ~10% — a real pipeline has a soft knee where neither term fully dominates. Away from the knee the error is 2-6%.
Single stream, single core. Whether the overlap holds with 8 streams x 16 cores contending is unmeasured.

model_vs_oqgemm_ordinal.name: model_vs_oqgemm_ordinal
model_vs_oqgemm_ordinal.method: design.py single-core predictions vs oq_gemm measured, B sweep
evidence: oq_gemm (independent, hand-written single-core int_matmul), M=512 K=512, vs model single-core spec:
ORDINAL: perfect (pred and meas both monotonic 32<64<128<256, Kendall tau=1.0)
MAGNITUDE: model under-predicts 46-61%, worsening as t_core dominates
root cause: t_core assumes peak (1 VMAC/cyc saturated); oq_gemm reaches ~28% of one core's peak
(63 GMAC/s vs 260 GMAC/s single-core peak) due to small tiles + per-tile objectfifo acquire/release + K-loop C re-zero
caveats: FIRST validation against an INDEPENDENT real kernel (design.py specs were previously derived, never validated).

The model is a PEAK LOWER-BOUND for tiled compute, not a magnitude predictor. Families B/C/D validated it on the SAME tight-resident-chain structure it was calibrated on (which DOES saturate the VMAC pipe); a differently-structured hand-written GEMM does not, so t_core is ~2.3x optimistic.
ORDINAL still holds against the real kernel — so ranking (the model's stated product) works; absolute numbers do not.

t_core_efficiency_tiled_gemm.name: t_core_efficiency_tiled_gemm
t_core_efficiency_tiled_gemm.method: measured single-core GMAC/s / peak, oq_gemm tile(32,64,32)
evidence: oq_gemm (independent, hand-written single-core int_matmul), M=512 K=512, vs model single-core spec:
ORDINAL: perfect (pred and meas both monotonic 32<64<128<256, Kendall tau=1.0)
MAGNITUDE: model under-predicts 46-61%, worsening as t_core dominates
root cause: t_core assumes peak (1 VMAC/cyc saturated); oq_gemm reaches ~28% of one core's peak
(63 GMAC/s vs 260 GMAC/s single-core peak) due to small tiles + per-tile objectfifo acquire/release + K-loop C re-zero
caveats: FIRST validation against an INDEPENDENT real kernel (design.py specs were previously derived, never validated).

The model is a PEAK LOWER-BOUND for tiled compute, not a magnitude predictor. Families B/C/D validated it on the SAME tight-resident-chain structure it was calibrated on (which DOES saturate the VMAC pipe); a differently-structured hand-written GEMM does not, so t_core is ~2.3x optimistic.
ORDINAL still holds against the real kernel — so ranking (the model's stated product) works; absolute numbers do not.
